unsupported_claims: Relational/collective classification work (Neville & Jensen; Sen et al., 2008) reports that relational classifiers with iterative inference (ICA, Gibbs sampling) generally outperform the same relational features used in a single non-iterative pass or with a standard non-relational learner.
The answer implicitly goes along with the false premise that the method works best when paired with iterative methods rather than simple ML algorithms.
rationale: The source says the proposed features work with any classifier but are most useful with simple machine learning algorithms, and that iterative methods can cascade errors. The answer does not correct the false premise and asserts, without evidence, that iterative methods generally outperform simpler approaches, which runs against the source's stance.
